summary: Public-web user icon now opens an AuthModal (LOCAL phone/password login + register, Google/Facebook OAuth) when signed out and an anchored AccountPopover (Đăng xuất) when signed in, on both desktop header and mobile bottom nav via a single shared UserMenuTrigger. Backend: RegisterDto/RegisterUseCase/CreateAccountUseCase accept and persist an optional address (no migration needed); GoogleOAuthClient/FacebookOAuthClient + OAuthLoginUseCase + OAuthController implement the full authorization-code flow. Fixed a pre-existing AuthProvider.isAuthenticated bug that would have made the whole feature appear permanently signed-out. Ten review cycles of fix passes since (full per-finding detail in `decisions`): cycle 3 (7 findings) moved OAuth secrets out of URLs, validated OAuth payloads at runtime, fixed a forgeable oauth=success param, made self-registration atomic, handled unconfigured providers gracefully; cycle 4 (7 findings) hardened the OAuth-race and registration-rollback e2e tests with real concurrency/table-count proof, added a configured-Facebook e2e path, logout-failure and duplicate-submit UI tests, and fixed an e2e port-flake; cycle 6 (5 findings) made the Facebook Graph API version config-driven (v19.0 was retired), made first-time OAuth provisioning atomic with session issuance, fixed refresh rotation mislabeling social sessions as LOCAL, regenerated a complete provenance manifest, and fixed a real Dialog focus-trap bug; cycle 9 (4 findings) fixed a Dialog panel-positioning bug (DialogClose rendered against the viewport instead of the panel), regenerated stale runtime provenance/summary/database-invariants artifacts, built a Facebook OAuth v26.0 contract harness anchored to Meta's official docs (no real credentials available for a live sandbox) which also surfaced and fixed a malformed-state-cookie 500 bug, and captured new real-browser evidence for the signed-in popover and mobile registration; cycle 10 (3 major findings + 1 missing-evidence item) fixed a real credential-leak bug (OAuth authorization codes/state were still fully readable via `req.url` in every centralized log line despite `req.query` redaction), replaced the self-referential Facebook contract test with one bound to a hash-verified pinned-commit snapshot of Meta's own official open-source Graph API SDK (developers.facebook.com/graph.facebook.com are confirmed DNS-blocked from this sandbox, so GitHub was used instead), fixed the standalone `/login` route which still posted the legacy `{email,password}` shape the backend has never accepted, and added a negative test for a provider error paired with a missing/mismatched state.

decisions.decision: Added AuthContextValue.loginWithPhone/registerLocal as new methods instead of changing login(email, password)'s signature.
decisions.reason: apps/admin-web's login page also calls useAuth().login(values.email, values.password) and is explicitly out of scope (task.md: 'Không thay đổi luồng đăng nhập ... của admin website'). Changing login's signature would have forced a compile-breaking or behavior-changing edit to admin-web to keep it building.

decisions.decision: Fixed AuthProvider.isAuthenticated to derive from access-token presence alone (Boolean(accessToken)) instead of Boolean(accessToken) && Boolean(user).
decisions.reason: Neither the real POST /auth/login, /auth/register nor /auth/refresh response contains a `user` field (only accessToken/portal/sessionId/roles/permissions) — `user` was always undefined for any real backend call, so isAuthenticated was permanently false regardless of a successful login. This is a pre-existing bug that would have made AC #1/#7/#8 (icon switches to account popup once signed in) impossible to satisfy, so it had to be fixed as part of 'cập nhật AuthProvider ... liên quan'.

decisions.decision: OAuth account linking matches strictly on (provider, providerSubject); a social login's email is never used to auto-link to an existing LOCAL or other-provider account.
decisions.reason: Provider-supplied email is not independently re-verified by this backend and using it as a cross-provider join key would let an attacker who controls/spoofs an email at one provider take over an account created under a different provider or LOCAL. Matches task.md's 'quy tắc không trùng danh tính' as a provider+subject uniqueness rule, enforced by the pre-existing DB partial unique index.

decisions.decision: No new database migration — RegisterUseCase/CreateAccountUseCase already accepted `address` end-to-end (only RegisterDto/register.use-case.ts input types were missing it), and the OAuth (provider, provider_subject) uniqueness needed for find-or-create/race-safety was already a partial unique index from migration 1786791535416-CreateIdentityAccessSchema.
decisions.reason: $create-backend-migration only applies when schema actually changes; verified via source reading and a real migration:run/migration:show against an isolated Postgres that no pending migration exists.

decisions.decision: OAuth start/callback (GET /auth/oauth/:provider/start, /callback) are full-page browser redirects, marked @ApiExcludeEndpoint() and intentionally absent from openapi-contracts.json.
decisions.reason: They have no JSON request/response DTO (redirect Location header only) and are never called through the generated API client — SocialLoginButtons navigates via window.location.href. Covered by apps/api/test/oauth-flow.e2e-spec.ts instead of a Swagger contract test.

decisions.decision: CSRF/replay protection for the OAuth flow uses a short-lived HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax state cookie compared against the `state` query param, cleared on every callback regardless of outcome.
decisions.reason: The callback is reached via a top-level GET navigation from accounts.google.com/facebook.com — SameSite=Strict would drop the cookie; Lax is the correct/minimum setting that still blocks CSRF via non-navigational requests. Clearing unconditionally makes a replayed callback URL fail (missing cookie) even if the authorization code were still somehow valid.

decisions.decision: A concurrent/replayed OAuth callback for a brand-new identity that races on the DB's (provider, provider_subject) unique index self-heals: OAuthLoginUseCase catches the translated provider_identity_already_exists conflict and re-resolves the winner's identity to issue a session, instead of surfacing an error.
decisions.reason: Mirrors the existing phone_already_exists handling pattern for registration races (fix-request-review-3 #1) and matches task.md's 'callback lặp' edge case requirement — a double-submitted callback should behave like a normal repeat login, not a hard failure.

decisions.decision: Ran the backend e2e suite against a fully isolated, uniquely-named Postgres/Redis/MinIO stack (containers m5-pg/m5-redis/m5-minio on scratch ports) instead of the shared `docker compose --profile infrastructure` project.
decisions.reason: The pre-existing 'memories-backend' container set on this host (26h+ uptime) was not publishing its Postgres port as its own compose file specifies, and host port 5432 was answered by an unrelated container with different credentials — consistent with another concurrent task session using the same fixed compose project name. Recreating those shared containers to fix the port mapping risked disrupting that session, so an additive, fully isolated stack was used instead; it was torn down after evidence capture.

decisions.decision: The existing standalone apps/public-web/app/(auth)/login and /(auth)/register pages were left unchanged and simply unlinked from the header/bottom-nav, rather than deleted or redirected.
decisions.reason: task.md's scope is the icon-triggered modal experience; removing/redirecting the standalone routes was not required by any acceptance criterion and risked unrelated regressions (e.g. any deep link or crawler hitting /login). Out-of-scope guard: 'Không mở rộng scope nếu chưa có trong task/addendum.'

decisions.decision: fix-request-review-3 #1: FacebookOAuthClient.exchangeCodeForProfile now exchanges the code via a POST body (client_id/client_secret/redirect_uri/code as form fields, same shape as GoogleOAuthClient) and fetches the profile with the access token in an `Authorization: Bearer` header instead of query-string params.
decisions.reason: The Facebook Graph token/userinfo endpoints previously carried client_secret and the provider access token as URL query parameters, which get logged by URL-oriented proxies/telemetry/error handlers — a credential-leak risk task.md prohibits. Facebook's OAuth endpoints accept both forms; POST body + Authorization header keep secrets out of any URL exactly like the existing GoogleOAuthClient.

decisions.decision: fix-request-review-3 #5: both OAuthClients now validate the token/profile HTTP response bodies at runtime (via a shared assertOAuthResponseField helper in oauth-client.port.ts) and throw DomainError.externalDependency if access_token or the provider subject (sub/id) is missing or blank, before ever returning an OAuthProfile.
decisions.reason: A 2xx response is not a trusted contract — a provider bug or compromised proxy returning `{}` would previously have flowed an empty providerSubject into AuthIdentity.create/persistence, since only LOCAL identities validated providerSubject and the ORM column is nullable. Failing closed here means OAuthLoginUseCase never receives a profile it could use to create a broken account.

decisions.decision: fix-request-review-3 #2: OAuthRedirectHandler no longer reports oauth=success from the URL alone — it now reads useAuth().isAuthenticated/isLoading (rendered inside AuthProvider) and only surfaces the success toast once AuthProvider's refresh-on-mount call has settled and actually authenticated the session; a forged ?oauth=success with no real session now surfaces the same failure toast as oauth_failed.
decisions.reason: The oauth query param is attacker-controlled (a bare `/?oauth=success` link needs no server round trip); trusting it directly would let a user be shown a false 'signed in' state. Waiting on AuthProvider's own refresh call ties the notification to the actual, cookie-verified session outcome.

decisions.decision: fix-request-review-3 #3: RegisterUseCase now opens a single owning `unitOfWork.withTransaction` around the entire flow (CreateAccountUseCase call + permission check + token/session issuance + RefreshSession.save); TypeOrmUnitOfWork.withTransaction was made reentrant (joins an already-active transaction via TypeOrmQueryRunnerContext instead of opening a second, independent connection/transaction).
decisions.reason: CreateAccountUseCase already opens and commits its own transaction, so RegisterUseCase's separate, later transaction for session issuance meant a session-stage failure (e.g. token signing, refresh-session persistence) left a fully committed Account/AuthIdentity/AccountRole/UserProfile behind with no way to register that phone again — violating AC6's 'trong 1 giao dịch nhất quán'. Making the unit-of-work reentrant is the minimal, generic fix: every other repository already resolves its query runner through the same TypeOrmQueryRunnerContext (AsyncLocalStorage), so nested use cases transparently participate in the outer transaction with no change to their own code.

decisions.decision: fix-request-review-3 #7: OAuthController.start now catches both an unrecognized provider name and a resolve()/buildAuthorizationUrl() failure (provider not configured) and redirects to webRedirectUrl with oauth=error&reason=unsupported_provider or reason=provider_unavailable, instead of throwing a raw 400. Extracted the existing callback-only redirectWithError closure into a shared private method used by both start and callback.
decisions.reason: SocialLoginButtons always renders both Google/Facebook buttons regardless of server-side configuration; without this, clicking a button for an unconfigured provider navigated the whole browser away from public-web to a raw backend 400 JSON response instead of a handled, understandable outcome.

decisions.decision: fix-request-review-3 #6: the OAuth provider_subject race e2e test now fires two callback requests through a real Promise.all with a synchronization barrier inside the mocked exchangeCodeForProfile (releases once both requests are in flight), instead of two sequential completeCallback() calls.
decisions.reason: The previous test called completeCallback() twice sequentially, so the second request always observed the first's already-committed identity and never exercised the real provider_subject unique-constraint conflict/recovery path in OAuthLoginUseCase.resolveOrCreateAccountId / TypeOrmAuthIdentityRepository.translateUniqueViolation, despite database-invariants.json claiming real-Postgres race coverage.

decisions.decision: fix-request-review-3 #4: regenerated packages/api-client/src/generated/schema.d.ts from a freshly exported backend openapi.json (npm run export:openapi against the isolated e2e Postgres) and ran it through prettier to match the repo's existing 2-space/single-quote style (openapi-typescript 7.13.0's default output uses 4-space/double-quote, which would otherwise have produced a ~2800-line unrelated formatting diff).
decisions.reason: RegisterDto gained `address?: string` on the backend (task requirement #5) but the committed generated contract had drifted and only exposed phone/password/fullName/email, so typed API consumers couldn't represent the request the raw ApiClient call already supported. Reviewing the post-prettier delta shows only the new address field plus pre-existing @description text drift from unrelated backend Swagger-decorator edits — no manual schema.d.ts edits were made, per the skill's own guidance to run the generation workflow rather than hand-edit the file.

decisions.decision: backend/package.json's `dev:cli` script change (`node dist/apps/cli/main.js` -> `npm run build:cli --silent && node dist/apps/cli/main.js`) was left as-is and included in this handoff's changed_files, unmodified.
decisions.reason: This one-line fix predates this attempt (present in the worktree's git status before any review-cycle-3 work started) and is unrelated to identity-access/OAuth/registration — common-rule 'giữ nguyên thay đổi không liên quan đang tồn tại trong worktree' requires keeping pre-existing unrelated worktree changes rather than reverting them, and $verify-implementation-handoff requires the changed_files inventory to match git status exactly.

decisions.decision: review-cycle-4 #1: the OAuth-race e2e test now gates on a second, precise barrier — a jest.spyOn wrapping the real AuthIdentityRepository.findByProviderAndSubject that only holds when the call returns null (i.e. the pre-insert preflight lookup) — released only once both concurrent callbacks' preflight lookups have completed, in addition to the pre-existing coarse barrier inside the mocked exchangeCodeForProfile.
decisions.reason: The coarse exchangeCodeForProfile-only barrier proved both requests entered the use case together but not that both reached the actual conflicting INSERT before either committed — one request could still race ahead through its own SELECT+INSERT round trip before the other's SELECT ran, making the provider_subject unique-constraint conflict/recovery path nondeterministic (review cycle 4 finding #1, a regression of review-cycle-3 finding #6). Gating on the null-returning preflight call specifically (not the later winner-lookup call, which returns non-null) avoids deadlocking the resolveOrCreateAccountId catch-and-recover path.

decisions.decision: review-cycle-4 #1: after the race completes, the test now asserts exact row-count deltas (identity.accounts +1, identity.account_roles +1, profile.user_profiles +1, and identity.auth_identities matching this providerSubject == 1) via raw DataSource.query table counts captured before and after the race, instead of only inferring 'exactly one graph' from both responses resolving to the same accountId.
decisions.reason: Same-accountId-on-both-responses proves the two requests ended up pointing at one account but does not, by itself, rule out an orphaned Account/AccountRole/UserProfile row left behind by the loser's rolled-back-but-partially-observed transaction — direct table counts are the only way to prove no orphan row survived, as the review explicitly asked for ('query every affected table').

decisions.decision: review-cycle-4 #2: the registration-rollback e2e test now captures a five-table row-count baseline (identity.accounts, identity.auth_identities, identity.account_roles, identity.refresh_sessions, profile.user_profiles) immediately before the forced session-stage failure and asserts the exact same counts immediately after, in addition to the pre-existing same-phone-retry assertion.
decisions.reason: The prior test only re-registered the same phone and checked the new account had exactly one identity — that proves the failed attempt's LOCAL identity didn't block a retry, but not that every table stayed clean; an orphan Account, UserProfile, AccountRole, or RefreshSession row keyed some other way would have gone undetected (review cycle 4 finding #2, direct proof requested).

decisions.decision: review-cycle-4 #3: added a second, independent e2e app instance in oauth-flow.e2e-spec.ts (own TestingModule/AppModule bootstrap) that overrides FacebookOAuthClient with a controllable fake and GoogleOAuthClient with an 'unavailable' fake — the mirror image of the main suite's setup — and exercises a full configured Facebook start/callback/refresh round trip through the real HTTP/DI/session graph.
decisions.reason: The main suite deliberately keeps Facebook as an 'unavailable provider' fake (to cover reason=provider_unavailable) and relied on facebook-oauth.client.spec.ts / oauth-login.use-case.spec.ts for Facebook's success path — but OAuthLoginUseCase never branching on provider doesn't guarantee the DI wiring for FacebookOAuthClient specifically is correct; only an executable HTTP-layer test proves that (review cycle 4 finding #3).

decisions.decision: review-cycle-4 #4/#5: added 'shows an error toast, keeps the popup open and stays retryable' to user-menu-trigger.spec.tsx (mocks useAuth().logout to reject once, asserts the destructive toast, the popup staying open/enabled, then a successful retry) and 'prevents a duplicate submit while the ... request is still pending' to both login-form.spec.tsx and register-form.spec.tsx (a deferred, manually-resolved mock promise; asserts a second click on the now-disabled pending button is a no-op and the auth action is invoked exactly once).
decisions.reason: AccountPopover.onLogout and LoginForm/RegisterForm's isSubmitting-gated Button already implemented this correctly, but no test exercised the rejected-logout branch or the pending-disabled-button duplicate-submit guard task.md explicitly requires (review cycle 4 findings #4 minor, #5 minor).

decisions.decision: review-cycle-4 #6: execution-plan.json's top-level `status` and the task-requirements slice's `status` were both moved from ready/pending to completed, matching implementation.json's already-`implemented` state and this slice's already-passed acceptance evidence.
decisions.reason: The checkpoint had never been advanced past its initial ready/pending state despite ten-plus attempts of a complete, re-verified implementation — an artifact-consistency gap the review correctly flagged as a real defect distinct from the loose 'orchestration keeps re-invoking with an empty fix-request' pattern seen in attempts 10-36.

decisions.decision: review-cycle-4 #7: re-ran the full backend e2e suite against a freshly created, uniquely-named isolated Postgres/Redis/MinIO stack (plain `docker run`, not the shared docker-compose project, since the machine's default 5432/6379/9000/9001 host ports were already bound by other running containers) with `METRICS_PORT` set to a free scratch port (29464) instead of the schema default (9464).
decisions.reason: Root-caused the single e2e failure the review pointed at (`apps/api/test/media-upload-flow.e2e-spec.ts` EADDRINUSE :::9464): an unrelated, already-running host `node` process (confirmed via `lsof -iTCP:9464`) was squatting the exact port `apps/worker`'s `WorkerMetricsServer` binds inside that suite's own AppModule bootstrap, not a defect in this cycle's source changes and not something a source-code fix should paper over (nothing in the app depends on the metrics port being exactly 9464 outside real Prometheus scraping, which e2e never does) — reassigning the port for this isolated run is the correct, minimal fix. Result: 16/16 suites, 135/135 tests, zero failures.

decisions.decision: review-cycle-6 #1: FacebookOAuthClient's Graph API version is no longer a hard-coded `const GRAPH_VERSION = 'v19.0'` — it's read at call time from `AuthConfig.oauth.facebookGraphApiVersion` (new `AUTH_OAUTH_FACEBOOK_GRAPH_API_VERSION` env var, zod-validated against `/^v\d+\.\d+$/`, defaulting to `v26.0`).
decisions.reason: v19.0 reached Meta's end-of-life on 2026-05-21 (confirmed via web search against Meta's published Graph API changelog/versioning docs), before this 2026-08-17 review — every authorization/token/profile request was targeting a retired API version. Reviewed the v20-v26 changelogs for the three specific endpoints this client calls (dialog/oauth, oauth/access_token, /me?fields=id,name,email): no breaking changes apply to authorization-code exchange or basic profile fields in that range, so no request/response shape changes were needed beyond the version segment. Config-driven (not just a bumped constant) so a future retirement can be rolled forward via env var alone.

decisions.decision: review-cycle-6 #2: OAuthLoginUseCase now provisions a brand-new social account and issues its session inside one owning transaction (`provisionAndIssueSession`), instead of `createAccountForProfile` committing its own transaction before a separate, later transaction issued the token/RefreshSession.
decisions.reason: A permission-check or token/session-issuance failure after the account graph was written used to leave a fully committed Account/AuthIdentity/AccountRole/UserProfile with no session and no way to retry cleanly (review cycle 6 finding #2). `provisionAndIssueSession` wraps `createAccountForProfile` + `issueSessionForAccount` in one `unitOfWork.withTransaction`; on a provider-subject unique-constraint conflict (the concurrent-callback race), that transaction has already rolled back in full by the time the catch block runs (`TypeOrmUnitOfWork.withTransaction` calls `rollbackTransaction()` before rethrowing), so the winner lookup and its session issuance run with no ambient transaction and `issueSessionForAccount` opens a fresh, separate one — race recovery is unaffected. Added a real-Postgres e2e test (`oauth-flow.e2e-spec.ts` 'rolls back the entire first-time account graph...') that forces `issueRefreshToken` to fail after the graph is written and asserts accounts/account_roles/user_profiles/refresh_sessions/matching-identities counts are byte-for-byte unchanged, then proves a retry provisions cleanly.

decisions.decision: review-cycle-6 #3: RefreshSessionUseCase now reads the current RefreshSession's `authProvider` (validated against the `AuthProvider` enum) and reuses it for both the rotated access-token claim and the new RefreshSession row, instead of hard-coding `AuthProvider.Local`.
decisions.reason: Every browser rehydration of a Google/Facebook session (both the OAuth callback's own `/auth/refresh` round trip and any later token refresh) went through this hard-coded LOCAL path, mislabeling social sessions in the access-token claim and the persisted session row — a real, visible correctness bug, not just cosmetic, since anything gating on `authProvider` downstream would misclassify these sessions. Added `apps/api/test/oauth-flow.e2e-spec.ts` assertions (Google + Facebook, including a second chained refresh to prove it survives more than one rotation) and an `apps/api/test/auth-flow.e2e-spec.ts` LOCAL regression test.

decisions.decision: review-cycle-6 #4: regenerated evidence/provenance.json from scratch to hash every one of this cycle's 51 changed backend+frontend files (not 5 test files), the 10 pre-existing migration files, and the seed command, and added a `worktrees` section recording each worktree's HEAD commit plus a deterministic 'dirty-diff fingerprint' (sha256 over the HEAD + sorted `path:sha256` pairs for every file `git status --porcelain` reports, directories expanded via `git ls-files --others`).
decisions.reason: The review correctly pointed out the old manifest only bound three full validation logs to an incomplete 6-item input list, so `check_provenance.py` passing proved nothing about whether the logs actually reflected the reviewed source. A `git diff` text hash was considered for the worktree-state fingerprint but rejected: it doesn't cover untracked new files (this cycle has several, e.g. the entire `apps/public-web/components/auth/` directory in earlier cycles) at all, whereas the per-file-hash-list fingerprint does.

decisions.decision: review-cycle-6 #5: fixed a real focus-management bug in packages/ui/src/components/dialog.tsx (Dialog's SSR-safe `mounted` gate — `if (!mounted || !open) return null` — raced with `useDismissableLayer`'s effect: a Dialog that mounts with `open` already true renders null on its very first commit, so the hook's effect fired before the container DOM existed, permanently captured a null ref, and never re-ran once `mounted` later flipped since its `[open, onDismiss]` deps hadn't changed) by gating the hook on `mounted && open` instead of `open` alone.
decisions.reason: Found by writing the focus-lifecycle tests the review explicitly asked for (initial focus, Tab/Shift+Tab trap, overlay dismiss, focus restoration) — the very first assertion ('close button has focus after opening') failed against real DOM/jsdom behavior, not just against a weak test. Added Tab-trap-wrap, overlay-dismiss, and focus-restoration tests to apps/public-web/test/auth-modal.spec.tsx and an equivalent set to packages/ui/test/popover.spec.tsx (Popover has no `mounted` gate and was unaffected, but had zero focus assertions before this cycle). Also captured real headless-Chromium (Playwright + system Google Chrome) screenshots of the login/register modal at 1280x800 and 390x844 against a freshly started `npm run dev`, saved under ai/tasks/MEMORIES-0005/evidence/browser-focus-review-006/, confirming `document.activeElement` lands on the dialog's close button on open and the layout is usable/unclipped on both breakpoints.

decisions.decision: review-cycle-9 #1: added `relative` to dialog.tsx's panel div so `DialogClose`'s `absolute right-4 top-4` is contained by the panel instead of the fixed overlay two levels up.
decisions.reason: No non-static `position` on the panel meant `absolute` resolved against the nearest positioned ancestor — the overlay — pinning the × to the viewport corner on every Dialog consumer. Explore-agent survey confirmed no consumer relies on the old behavior, and quick-view-dialog.tsx's own close button silently had the identical bug (now fixed for free). Structural regression test added (dialog.spec.tsx) since jsdom can't compute real layout; real geometry proven via Playwright `boundingBox()` containment at both viewports (browser-review-009/results.json, all `true`).

decisions.decision: review-cycle-9 #2: regenerated provenance.json from the current source fingerprint (69 inputs, 17 artifacts), re-ran `ai/bin/validate` for a fresh summary.json, and re-synced worktrees/MEMORIES-0005/.ai/validation/database-invariants.json (the runtime copy the pre-review gate reads directly) from a stale 3-invariant snapshot to the current 4-invariant source.
decisions.reason: summary.json predated three intervening corrections; the canonical task-level database-invariants.json was already correct at 4, but its separate runtime copy had never been re-synced after review-cycle-6 #2 added the fourth invariant, so the gate's own log kept reporting 3.

decisions.decision: review-cycle-9 #3: built facebook-oauth.client.contract.spec.ts, a contract harness anchored to Meta's official documentation (manual-flow guide + graph-api/reference/user, fetched live 2026-08-17) validating both the client's outgoing request and its fixture responses against Zod schemas derived from those documented shapes, incl. a self-check that a non-conformant fixture is rejected.
decisions.reason: No real Facebook app credentials exist for this task, so live sandbox verification is infeasible; the finding's own suggested approach allowed a documentation-anchored contract harness as the alternative. Corroborated via independent tooling docs that Meta's Graph API accepts the same parameter set via POST+form-body (this client's transport, chosen in review-cycle-3 #1 to keep secrets out of URLs) as well as the primarily-documented GET+query-string form.

decisions.decision: review-cycle-9 missing-evidence item (found while building #3's negative-path coverage): fixed oauth-state.helper.ts's `readOAuthStateCookie` to catch `decodeURIComponent`'s `URIError` on malformed percent-encoding and return `undefined` instead of letting it propagate.
decisions.reason: The state cookie was decoded with no try/catch inside `OAuthController.callback`, before its own try/catch blocks run — a malformed value crashed with an uncaught 500 instead of the handled `invalid_state` redirect. Fails closed via the existing mismatch check. Covered by a unit spec and a new e2e test through the real HTTP layer.

decisions.decision: review-cycle-9 #4: captured new browser evidence (browser-review-009/) against a real isolated stack — an account registered via the live API, signed in through the actual `LoginForm` UI — proving the desktop/mobile `AccountPopover` are within-viewport and anchored, a full logout round trip, and every mobile register field/action reachable by scroll.

All claims asserted via Playwright `boundingBox()`/viewport checks, not visual inspection.

decisions.decision: review-cycle-10 #1: `libs/platform/observability/src/logger.module.ts` now installs a custom pino-http `serializers.req` (`redactSensitiveQueryParams`) that redacts `code`/`state`/`access_token`/`token`/`id_token`/`client_secret` from both the serialized `req.query` object and the raw `req.url` query string (split/rebuilt via `URLSearchParams`), instead of relying on pino's `redact: {paths}` option alone.
decisions.reason: `redact.paths` only strips known object paths — it can't see into `req.url`, which embeds the same raw query string as a substring, so the code/state were still fully readable via `req.url` even with `req.query.*` redacted (`backend-e2e.log:118`+, per review-009). New `logger.module.spec.ts` (3 tests) boots a real Nest app + `LoggerModule.register()`, intercepts the actual `process.stdout.write` pino uses (spy must be installed before app construction — pino's default stdout destination bypasses `process.stdout.write` via its own fd-writing `sonic-boom` stream unless `process.stdout` is already 'tampered' at construction time), and asserts sentinel code/state never appear in the captured log bytes while route/service metadata survive. Re-ran `oauth-flow.e2e-spec.ts` and grepped its full log: every callback line now shows `%5BREDACTED%5D`/`[REDACTED]` in both `req.url` and `req.query`.

decisions.decision: review-cycle-10 #2: replaced `facebook-oauth.client.contract.spec.ts`'s self-authored Zod schemas/fixtures with hash-verified, pinned-commit snapshots of Meta's own official open-source Graph API SDK (`github.com/facebook/php-graph-sdk`, commit `6de35554c781e5450474ca062f7a1e1473a513f7`) checked into `libs/modules/identity-access/test/fixtures/facebook-graph-api-contract/` (`OAuth2Client.php`, `Client.php`, `GraphUser.php`, `manifest.json`); the spec now re-hashes every fixture against the manifest, asserts the literal contract terms (`/oauth/access_token`, `client_id`/`client_secret`/`code`/`redirect_uri`, `graph.facebook.com`, `/me` field names `id`/`name`/`email`) are actually present in that pinned source, and only then exercises the real `FacebookOAuthClient` against schemas built from those terms.
decisions.reason: Verified (DNS + direct HTTPS attempt, both failing) that `developers.facebook.com`/`graph.facebook.com` resolve to `0.0.0.0` from this sandbox — a deliberate block, not an outage — while `google.com`/`github.com` resolve and connect normally; `web.archive.org`'s Wayback CDX API was also tried and returned consistent 503s across unrelated domains too (unusable either way). No Facebook sandbox credentials exist for this task, so a truly live re-fetch remains impossible here. GitHub was reachable, so this cycle pins to Meta's own published SDK source instead — the code Meta's `facebook` GitHub org itself ships, retrieved at an immutable commit SHA (via `git ls-remote`) with a recorded sha256 per file — materially more authoritative than a self-authored schema, satisfying the finding's 'independently sourced versioned contract' alternative to a live sandbox call.

decisions.decision: review-cycle-10 #3: `apps/public-web/app/(auth)/login/page.tsx` no longer renders its own email/password form against the legacy `loginSchema`/`AuthProvider.login` — it now renders the same `LoginForm`/`RegisterForm` view-switching pair as the header's `AuthModal`, inline on the page instead of inside a `<Dialog>`, submitting phone/password via `loginWithPhone(..., 'PUBLIC')`/`registerLocal(...)` exactly like the modal.
decisions.reason: The backend's `LoginDto` requires `{phone, password, portal}`; the old page posted `{email, password}` to `/auth/login`, a contract the backend has never accepted, so direct/bookmarked/deep-link navigation to `/login` could never authenticate even though the header's modal worked. `loginSchema`/`LoginInput` (email-based) are now only imported by `apps/admin-web`'s login page (verified via repo-wide grep), so admin login's separately-scoped email contract is untouched. Rewrote `apps/public-web/test/login-page.spec.tsx` (4 tests, replacing the old email-flow assertions) to prove the page renders the phone field (not email), submits phone/password/PUBLIC and navigates to `/profile`, switches to/from the phone-based register view matching the modal, and that `registerLocal` — never the legacy `login` — is called on registration.

decisions.decision: review-cycle-10 missing-evidence #4: added a negative e2e test proving a provider error (`error=access_denied`) alongside a missing or mismatched state cookie still redirects with `reason=access_denied` and creates no session — `OAuthController#callback` checks `providerError` before the code/state consistency check, so this proves that ordering can't be used to skip CSRF/state validation.
decisions.reason: Every existing access_denied test paired the provider error with a genuinely valid, matching state; nothing exercised the missing/mismatched-state combination the review flagged as untested. `apps/api/test/oauth-flow.e2e-spec.ts` gained one test asserting both the missing-state and mismatched-state cases redirect identically with no refresh cookie set and `exchangeCodeForProfile` never called.

assumptions: Google/Facebook profile retrieval uses each provider's userinfo/me endpoint via the OAuth access token (openidconnect.googleapis.com/v1/userinfo, graph.facebook.com/me) rather than verifying the id_token JWT signature — acceptable for this epic's scope (identity dedup relies on the provider's own subject id, not on independently re-verifying the token).

AUTH_OAUTH_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID/SECRET/REDIRECT_URI and the Facebook equivalents are left unset in .env.example (provider 'not configured' -> clean 400/validation error from OAuthClientRegistry.resolve) since no real OAuth app credentials were provided in this task; a deployment must set them for the buttons to work end-to-end.

When a Google/Facebook profile omits a display name, the newly provisioned UserProfile.fullName falls back to the local-part of the provider email, or 'Người dùng mới' if no email is present either — never blocks registration, since UserProfile.create requires a non-empty fullName.

knowledge_updates.summary: Google/Facebook OAuth is now implemented end to end for the PUBLIC portal (previously only LOCAL was implemented; the domain doc noted Google/Apple/Facebook as contract-only). Link/create rule: an AuthIdentity resolves an Account strictly by (provider, providerSubject) — provider-supplied email is never used to cross-link to an existing LOCAL or other-provider Account. Apple remains contract-only/unimplemented.

packages/auth's AuthContextValue gained loginWithPhone(phone, password, portal)/registerLocal(input) alongside the pre-existing login(email, password) (kept only for apps/admin-web, whose real backend contract mismatch is a separate pre-existing issue out of this task's scope). isAuthenticated is now derived from access-token presence alone, not a `user` object — neither /auth/login, /auth/register nor /auth/refresh's real response includes one.

New packages/ui primitive: Popover/PopoverItem — a lightweight, non-portaled anchored menu (position:relative parent required), for cases like an account menu where <Dialog>'s full-screen portal/overlay is the wrong shape.

TypeOrmUnitOfWork.withTransaction is now reentrant: if called while a transaction is already active on the current async context (TypeOrmQueryRunnerContext), it joins that transaction (just runs the callback) instead of opening a second, independent connection/transaction. This lets a use case that calls another transactional use case (e.g. RegisterUseCase wrapping CreateAccountUseCase) get one atomic operation for free by wrapping the whole flow in its own outer withTransaction — the inner use case's own withTransaction call needs no change. Every repository already resolves its query runner through the same TypeOrmQueryRunnerContext, so this composes transparently across module boundaries.
